title: Malaysia | BNM Governance, Responsibility Mapping, Whistleblowing and Harassment
tagline: Lead and work in a Malaysian bank the way BNM expects: a challenging board, fit and proper people, named owners, safe speak-up channels and respect at work.
sectors: All bank staff, contractors and interns
description:
A Malaysia-specific governance and conduct quest for conventional licensed banks. It is based on the **Financial Services Act 2013** (sections 54 to 62) and Bank Negara Malaysia's (BNM) policy documents on **Corporate Governance** (2016), **Fit and Proper Criteria** (2013) and **Responsibility Mapping** (in force from 1 January 2026), BNM's whistleblowing channel and Enforcement Approach, and the sexual harassment provisions of the **Employment Act 1955** (Part XVA, including the section 81H awareness notice) and the **Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022**.

BNM requires every bank to have a whistleblowing policy that staff, contractors, consultants and interns know how to use, requires directors to commit to ongoing education and senior managers to understand and acknowledge what they are accountable for, and employers must raise awareness of sexual harassment and inquire into complaints. This quest supports those duties for directors, senior management, managers, HR and governance teams, and all staff, and uses two real BNM enforcement cases.

It builds knowledge of the Malaysian framework and does not replace your bank's own policies, procedures or legal advice. Islamic banking requirements are outside its scope.
audience: Directors and board committee members of Malaysian licensed banks
CEOs, senior officers and other key responsible persons named in a responsibility map
Company secretaries, governance, compliance and internal audit teams
HR, employee relations and line managers who receive whistleblowing reports or harassment complaints
All bank employees, contractors, consultants and interns who need to know how to speak up safely
outcomes: Explain the board's and directors' duties under FSA sections 56 to 58 and BNM's composition and independence rules
Apply the FSA and BNM fit and proper requirements, including approvals, disqualification, annual assessment and director development
Build and use a responsibility map that meets BNM's four principles, with written acknowledgements
Use and protect whistleblowing channels inside the bank and to BNM, and recognise reprisal
Handle sexual harassment complaints under Part XVA of the Employment Act and know the Tribunal route under the 2022 Act
Describe how BNM enforces governance requirements and what evidence a governance review will look for

quest.name: The Selasih Compass
quest.premise: You have just joined the Governance Office of Selasih Bank Berhad, a fictional conventional bank headquartered in Kuala Lumpur with branches from Penang to Johor Bahru. BNM's supervisors arrive in six weeks for a governance and culture review, the first since Responsibility Mapping took effect. With Haslina, Vikram, Dr Margaret, Amirul and Jia Hui, clear five stages from the Board Room to the Review Hall, then face the final boss: the supervisors' questions.

sessions.title: The Board: FSA Duties, Composition, Independence and Committees
sessions.summary: How the Financial Services Act and BNM's Corporate Governance policy document shape a Malaysian bank's board: directors' duties, the board charter, independence tests, committees, conflicts of interest and minutes that show challenge.
objectives: Explain the board's duties under FSA section 56 and each director's duties under section 57
Apply BNM's rules on board composition, the chairman, executive directors and independence
Handle a director's interest in a material transaction under section 58 and paragraph 14
Describe the four required board committees and what good minutes must record

cards.title: Six weeks to the governance review
cards.setting: Governance Office, Selasih Bank Berhad head office, Kuala Lumpur. Monday, 8:30 am.

lines.text: Your first morning in the Governance Office of Selasih Bank Berhad, a fictional conventional bank with branches from Penang to Johor Bahru. The board papers trolley is already full.
Welcome! I'm Haslina Othman, Company Secretary and Head of Governance, and your mentor. Big news: BNM's supervisors will run a governance and culture review here in six weeks.
Vikram Pillai, Chief Compliance Officer. It's the first review since Responsibility Mapping took effect in January 2026. They will ask who owns what, and whether people can speak up safely.
Dr Margaret Chong, independent director and chair of the nominations committee. They will also test the board. Can we show real challenge, or only signatures?
So the quest has five stages: the board, fitness and propriety, responsibility mapping, speaking up, and respect at work. Stage 1 starts in the board room.
First question for you: who actually runs a bank in Malaysia, the board or the CEO?

cards.title: The governance rulebook for a Malaysian bank

scenes.heading: The Financial Services Act 2013
scenes.narration: The Financial Services Act 2013 is the base law for licensed conventional banks. Its Part on governance covers the board, directors' duties, disqualification and fit and proper requirements.

scenes.heading: BNM's Corporate Governance policy document
scenes.narration: Bank Negara Malaysia issued its Corporate Governance policy document on 3 August 2016 under sections 47 and 58 of the Act. It sets board, senior management, culture and disclosure standards.

scenes.heading: Three companion documents
scenes.narration: It works with the Fit and Proper Criteria policy document of 2013, the Responsibility Mapping policy document in force from 1 January 2026, and the bank's own policies.

scenes.heading: S means must
scenes.narration: Paragraphs marked S are standards that must be met, and breaches can lead to enforcement action. Paragraphs marked G are guidance that BNM encourages.

scenes.heading: Scope of this quest
scenes.narration: We cover conventional licensed banks. Islamic banking rules sit in a separate Act and are outside this quest.

cards.title: From statute to the board table
cards.caption: BNM looks for evidence at every layer, especially effective challenge of management on key strategic decisions.

items.label: FSA 2013, Part on governance
items.detail: Sections 54 to 62 set approvals, board and director duties, disqualification and fit and proper rules.

items.label: BNM policy documents
items.detail: Corporate Governance, Fit and Proper Criteria and Responsibility Mapping add binding detail.

items.label: Board charter
items.detail: Each board must have a charter setting its mandate, committees and matters reserved for its decision.

items.label: Board and committee practice
items.detail: Agendas, papers, challenge, minutes and evaluations show whether the rules work in reality.

cards.question: Under section 56 of the Financial Services Act 2013, how is the business of a licensed bank managed?
options: Directly by the board, which must approve every credit decision
Under the direction and oversight of the board of directors
By the CEO alone, with the board acting only as an adviser
By Bank Negara Malaysia through its supervisors
cards.explanation: Section 56(1) places the business and affairs of the institution under the direction and oversight of its board. Management runs the bank day to day, but within the board's direction.

cards.title: Four personal duties of every director
Board versus senior management
cards.caption: Paragraph 16.1 also makes senior management responsible for dealing with actual or suspected breaches promptly.

items.label: Core role
items.left: Direction and oversight; hold management to account
items.right: Day-to-day management led by the CEO

items.label: Strategy and risk
items.left: Approves risk appetite and business plans
items.right: Implements strategy within the risk appetite

items.label: People
items.left: Oversees selection, pay and succession of CEO and control heads
items.right: Builds a structure with clear accountability

items.label: Culture
items.left: Sets the tone from the top with management
items.right: Promotes the same culture in daily decisions

items.label: Information
items.left: Must receive what it needs to oversee
items.right: Must report breaches, control failures and supervisory concerns

cards.title: Independent or not?
cards.prompt: Paragraph 11.7 lists situations that rule out independence. Sort each candidate.

items.text: Retired from the bank's executive committee 18 months ago
Spouse holds 6% of the bank's shares
Law firm partner whose firm earned large fees from the bank last year
Retired judge with no business link to the bank or its group
Former executive who left the bank four years ago
Academic who holds a small savings account at a branch
Accountant whose firm has had a significant contract with a group affiliate in the past two years

lines.text: We have a strong candidate for an independent seat: Encik Faizal, a former deputy CEO of our own leasing subsidiary. He left 20 months ago.
Then he was an executive of an affiliate within the last two years. Paragraph 11.7 says he cannot be counted as independent yet.
He could still join as a non-independent director, but the board must keep a majority of independent directors at all times.
And remember the definition of 'linked' persons. If his brother runs one of our key IT vendors, that matters too.
Right. Independence is a test of character and judgement, plus a set of bright-line exclusions. Both must be passed.

cards.title: The director with an interest
cards.situation: At Thursday's board meeting the agenda includes a RM40 million property lease for the new Penang regional office. Ten minutes before the meeting, director Datuk Ramli mentions to Haslina that his family company owns the building. He has not told the board in writing. What should Haslina advise?

choices.text: Ask him to give written notice of the nature and extent of his interest to all directors and the company secretary before the item starts, and to leave the meeting while it is deliberated.
choices.outcome: Correct. Section 58 requires disclosure and absence during deliberation of a material transaction, and paragraph 14.3 requires written notice to all board members and the company secretary before the deliberation begins. The minutes should record his absence.

choices.text: Let him stay but abstain from the vote, since everyone already knows about the family company.
choices.outcome: Not enough. Section 58(2) says an interested director must not be present while the material transaction is deliberated, and paragraph 14.3 still requires written notice even when other directors already know.

choices.text: Defer the item to the next meeting so he can prepare a formal declaration.
choices.outcome: Deferral may be sensible if the papers are incomplete, but it does not by itself deal with the conflict. The disclosure and absence rules still apply whenever the item is discussed.

choices.text: Tell him an oral mention to the chairman is sufficient because he is not voting.
choices.outcome: Wrong. BNM specifies written notice to all members of the board and the company secretary. An oral word to the chairman leaves no record and does not meet the standard.

cards.title: The numbers behind a sound board
cards.caption: Source: BNM Corporate Governance policy document, paragraphs 9, 11 and 12.

items.label: Meeting attendance
items.detail: Minimum share of board meetings each director must attend every financial year.

items.label: Quorum
items.detail: At least half of the board members must be present.

items.label: Independence
items.detail: Independent directors must be a majority of the board at all times.

items.label: Tenure expectation
items.detail: BNM expects independent director tenure generally not to exceed nine years.

items.label: Committee size
items.detail: Each required board committee has at least three directors, mostly independent.

items.label: Look-back period
items.detail: Recent executives or significant business links in this period bar independence.

cards.title: Four committees, four jobs
cards.prompt: Match each required board committee to its main task (Appendix 1).

pairs.right: Supports appointments, composition, evaluations and fit and proper assessments of directors and senior management.
Oversees the design and operation of the remuneration system.
Supports the board on risk governance and checks that incentives reflect risk.
Oversees financial reporting, internal audit, the external auditor and related party transactions.
Remains fully accountable for anything it delegates to a committee.

cards.title: Board room rules you will be asked about

cards.front: Can a director send a substitute?
cards.back: No. A director must not appoint someone else to attend or take part in a board meeting on their behalf.
Allowed, but it should be the exception, with safeguards for confidentiality.
Decisions, key deliberations, the reason for each decision, significant concerns or dissent, and any abstentions.

cards.front: Who may chair a board committee?
cards.back: An independent director, and never the chairman of the board.
No more than one, unless BNM approves otherwise in writing.

cards.front: Can an active politician be a director?
cards.back: No. Paragraph 10.4 rules out active politicians.

cards.question: Which person could BNM's Corporate Governance policy document allow to chair Selasih Bank's board?
options: The current CEO, provided the board votes for it
A non-executive director who was the bank's CEO three years ago
A non-executive director who has never been an executive of the bank
The chair of the board audit committee, who would keep both roles
cards.explanation: The chairman must not be an executive and must not have been the CEO in the past five years, so the current or recent CEO is out. The board chairman also must not chair any board committee.

cards.title: Example: minutes that prove challenge
Supporting the board well
cards.body:
- Papers should reach directors early enough to read them; the chairman must make sure directors get relevant information on time.
- Flag the decision needed and the risks on page one.
- If directors need independent advice, the bank must provide access to third-party experts at its own cost.
- Record dissent accurately. A minute that hides disagreement protects nobody.

cards.title: Stage 1 take-aways
items: Section 56 of the FSA puts the bank under the direction and oversight of the board, which must regard depositors' interests.
Section 57 gives every director personal duties of good faith, care, proper purpose and independent judgement.
BNM requires a majority of independent directors, a non-executive chairman who was not CEO in the past five years, and four board committees.
Independence is lost by recent executive roles, substantial shareholdings or significant business links, including through linked persons.
Interested directors give written notice and leave the room while the material transaction is deliberated.
Minutes must show reasons, concerns and dissent so that challenge can be evidenced.

cards.prompt: Think of a decision forum you sit in or report to. Would its minutes show a supervisor that people challenged the proposal and why the decision was taken? What would you change?

quiz.question: Selasih Bank's board approves a new SME lending strategy. Which statement best reflects the board's duty under section 56 of the Financial Services Act 2013?
options: It must oversee the strategy with regard to long-term viability and reasonable standards of fair dealing
It may approve any strategy that maximises short-term profit for shareholders
It must manage the SME unit directly, approving each facility itself so that management cannot deviate from the plan
It needs to consider only BNM's capital rules, since fair dealing is left to management
quiz.explanation: Section 56(2)(a) requires the board to set and oversee business and risk strategies with regard to long-term viability and reasonable standards of fair dealing. Running the unit itself confuses oversight with management.

quiz.question: A director who is a former chief risk officer sits on Selasih's board. How is his duty of care measured under section 57?
options: Only against the minimum expected of an ordinary director, whatever extra background or experience he brings to the board
Only against the standard of a chief risk officer, as if he were still employed
It is not measured, because care is a collective duty of the whole board
Against what is expected of a director in that role, plus the extra knowledge and experience he actually has
quiz.explanation: Section 57(1)(b) sets two limbs: the knowledge, skill and experience reasonably expected of a director with the same responsibilities, and any additional knowledge and experience the director has.

quiz.question: What share of board meetings must each director attend in every financial year under BNM's Corporate Governance policy document?
options: At least 50%
At least two-thirds
At least 75%
At least 90%
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 9.3 requires attendance at a minimum of 75% of board meetings held in each financial year, and forbids sending someone else in the director's place.

quiz.question: Which candidate cannot be treated as an independent director of Selasih Bank?
options: A candidate who left a senior executive role at the bank five years ago
A candidate who holds a personal current account and a home loan on standard terms
A candidate who chaired a charity that the bank once sponsored with a small donation
A candidate whose husband holds 5% of the shares of a Selasih group affiliate
quiz.explanation: A person is not independent if they or a linked person (which includes relatives) is a substantial shareholder, meaning 5% or more, of the bank or its affiliates. The five-year-old executive role is outside the two-year look-back.

quiz.question: Selasih's board has eight directors. What is the minimum number of independent directors it must have at all times?
options: Four
Three
Five
Six
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11.6 requires a majority of independent directors at all times. With eight directors, four is only half, so at least five are needed.

quiz.question: Which arrangement for Selasih's board audit committee meets paragraph 12 of the Corporate Governance policy document?
options: Three non-executive directors, two of them independent, chaired by an independent director
Four directors, including the executive director and two independents, chaired by the chairman of the board
Two independent directors, chaired by the more senior of them
Three directors, mostly independent, chaired by a non-independent director
quiz.explanation: Each committee needs at least three directors, a majority of independent directors and an independent chair. The board chairman cannot chair a committee, and only the nominations committee may include an executive director.

quiz.question: Datuk Ramli's family company is bidding for a large contract with Selasih. Which step does section 58 of the FSA and paragraph 14.3 require of him?
options: Tell the chairman privately before the meeting, stay in the room and vote last so that the others are not influenced by him
Resign from the board before the tender is opened
Declare the interest only if the contract is finally awarded to his family company
Give written notice of his interest to every director and the company secretary, then stay out while it is deliberated
quiz.explanation: Section 58 requires disclosure of the nature and extent of the interest and absence while the material transaction is deliberated. Paragraph 14.3 makes the disclosure a written notice to all board members and the company secretary, before the deliberation starts.

quiz.question: BNM's supervisors read a year of Selasih board minutes and see only 'noted and approved'. Which concern are they most likely to raise?
options: There is no evidence that the board challenged management or why each decision was taken
The minutes are too short to be filed with the Companies Commission and must be expanded before the annual return
The board should have voted by secret ballot on every item
The minutes should have been signed by every director, not just the chairman
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 9.6 requires minutes to record key deliberations, the rationale for each decision and significant concerns or dissent, and BNM says it expects to see evidence of effective challenge.

quiz.question: Which statement about the role of senior management is consistent with paragraph 16.1 of the Corporate Governance policy document?
options: Management must deal with actual or suspected regulatory breaches promptly and keep the board informed
Management should report only breaches that BNM has already detected
Management sets the risk appetite, and the board then reviews it each year
Management may limit what the board sees to protect commercially sensitive data and avoid leaks from board papers
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 16.1 makes senior management responsible for addressing actual or suspected breaches in a timely way and for regularly giving the board material information, including on internal control failures and supervisory concerns. The board approves the risk appetite.

quiz.question: Selasih wants to appoint its long-serving CEO as board chairman when he retires next month. What does the Corporate Governance policy document say?
options: He may chair the board immediately if shareholders approve at a general meeting
He cannot become chairman until five years after he last served as CEO
He may chair the board if he also chairs the board risk management committee
He may become chairman after a two-year cooling-off period
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11.3 says the chairman must not be an executive and must not have served as CEO of the institution in the past five years. The two-year period applies to other tests, such as independence.

sessions.title: Fit and Proper: Approvals, Disqualification, Assessments and Director Development
sessions.summary: Who needs BNM's approval, who is disqualified, how banks assess probity, competence and financial integrity, what happens when someone stops being fit and proper, and how directors keep their skills current.
objectives: Identify appointments that need BNM's prior written approval and the application timeline
Distinguish section 59 disqualification from a section 60 fit and proper failure
Apply the three fit and proper criteria, the annual cycle and the seven-day notice rule
Explain BNM's expectations on director education, evaluation and development plans

cards.title: Two files on the desk
cards.setting: Nominations committee secretariat, Selasih Bank head office.

lines.text: Stage 2. Two files. One: our CEO retires in nine months and the successor application is not started. Two: a new independent director candidate with no technology background.
Amirul Zainal, Chief Human Resource Officer. And a third, unofficial file: one of our senior officers just told HR he has a court judgment against him for an unpaid personal loan.
Nine months is not long. BNM must approve the CEO in writing before appointment, and the application must go in at least three months ahead.
BNM has already fined an institution for leaving its CEO seat empty. Succession planning is not paperwork.
Today you learn the fit and proper machinery: who needs approval, who is disqualified, how we assess people, and how directors keep learning.

cards.title: Fit and proper in the Financial Services Act

scenes.heading: Prior approval
scenes.narration: Under section 54, a licensed bank needs BNM's prior written approval to appoint or reappoint its chairman, directors and CEO, and must have a CEO at all times.

scenes.heading: Automatic disqualification
scenes.narration: Section 59 disqualifies people such as undischarged bankrupts or anyone with a proven charge of dishonesty or fraud from being a chairman, director, CEO or senior officer.

scenes.heading: BNM sets the criteria
scenes.narration: Section 60 lets BNM specify fit and proper requirements on probity and integrity, competency and capability, and financial integrity. BNM has full discretion to decide disputes.

scenes.heading: Immediate exit
scenes.narration: Under section 61, a person who becomes disqualified or stops being fit and proper must immediately cease to act, and the bank must terminate or remove them.

scenes.heading: Tell BNM
scenes.narration: Section 62 requires the bank to notify BNM in writing, with reasons, within seven days after any of these people leave office for any reason.

cards.title: Appointing a director or CEO
cards.caption: Based on FSA section 54 and Corporate Governance paragraphs 10 and 17 and Appendix 3.

items.label: Board is wholly satisfied
items.detail: An objective assessment shows the candidate meets every minimum requirement and can contribute.

items.label: Application to BNM
items.detail: Submitted at least three months before the person should start, with the board's assessment.

items.label: Gaps explained
items.detail: For a director, the application explains skill gaps and how the board will support the candidate.

items.label: BNM written approval
items.detail: No public announcement of the appointment before approval is obtained.

items.label: Terms acknowledged
items.detail: The director acknowledges role, tenure and removal terms in writing.

cards.question: Which people at Selasih Bank are 'key responsible persons' under BNM's Fit and Proper Criteria policy document?
options: Directors, the CEO and senior officers
Only the directors and the company secretary
Every employee who has a credit approval limit
Only the CEO and the chief compliance officer
cards.explanation: For a conventional bank, key responsible persons are directors, the CEO and senior officers (members of a Shariah committee are added only for Islamic business). The company secretary is assessed under its own criteria but is not a senior officer.

cards.title: Three criteria, assessed honestly
cards.body:
The Fit and Proper Criteria policy document asks the board and nominations committee to weigh three groups of factors:

**1. Probity, personal integrity and reputation.** Has the person faced disciplinary or criminal proceedings, regulatory sanctions, dismissal over honesty questions, or links to failed or delicensed businesses? Have they been unwilling to cooperate with regulators or to keep effective controls?

**2. Competency and capability.** Do they have the qualifications, **training**, skills, practical experience and commitment for the role, and, for directors, enough time given other commitments? Is past performance satisfactory?

**3. Financial integrity.** Do they meet their own financial obligations? Is there an unsatisfied judgment debt? Limited means alone is not a failure.

Assessments happen **before appointment** and **at least annually**, and again whenever the bank learns something that may materially affect fitness. Factors are weighed individually and together; one failed factor does not automatically mean failure, but the reasons must be documented.

cards.title: Which criterion does it test?
cards.prompt: Place each piece of information under the fit and proper criterion it mainly goes to.

items.text: A past reprimand by a professional accounting body
Resigned from a previous bank after questions about expense claims
No experience in treasury, but nominated to head treasury
Holds six other directorships with heavy time demands
An unsatisfied court judgment for an unpaid personal loan
Repeatedly missed personal tax and loan repayments
Refused to give documents to a regulator in an earlier job
Strong record running a retail bank of similar size

cards.title: Real case: an empty CEO seat (BNM, 2026)

lines.text: Our Head of Payments Operations, Encik Shahrul, says a court gave judgment against him last year and it is still unpaid. He is a senior officer on our key responsible persons list.
Then we do not wait for the annual cycle. The policy document says to reassess whenever we learn something that may materially affect fitness and propriety.
Does that mean he is out?
Not automatically. A judgment debt is not one of the section 59 disqualifications. We weigh it with the other factors, check the facts independently, and record our reasoning.
And credit to him for telling us. Both the Corporate Governance document and our internal policy expect people to disclose such things straight away.

cards.title: A charge in court
cards.situation: Selasih's Head of Treasury has just been charged in court with an offence involving fraud, linked to a family business. The case may take two years. He insists he is innocent and wants to keep working as usual. What should the bank do?

choices.text: Stop him acting as Head of Treasury and from involvement in the bank's affairs unless the board permits otherwise on conditions BNM specifies, reassess his fitness, and escalate to BNM.
choices.outcome: Best answer. Section 59(2) says that while criminal proceedings for such an offence are pending, a senior officer must not act in that capacity or take part in the bank's business, except as the board permits subject to BNM's conditions. A reassessment and early engagement with BNM follow.

choices.text: Let him continue as normal, because he is innocent until proven guilty.
choices.outcome: Presumption of innocence applies in court, but the FSA sets its own rule for pending proceedings involving dishonesty or fraud. Carrying on as normal breaches section 59(2).

choices.text: Dismiss him immediately and notify BNM within seven days.
choices.outcome: Too fast and not what the law requires. A pending charge is not a proven charge, so he is not yet disqualified under section 59(1). The bank must restrict his role and reassess; dismissal may follow only on proper grounds.

choices.text: Ask him to work from home on treasury matters until the case ends.
choices.outcome: This keeps him involved in the bank's business, which section 59(2) does not allow without the board's permission under BNM's conditions.

cards.title: When a senior officer is no longer fit and proper
cards.prompt: Put the bank's steps in the order the FSA and the policy documents expect.
steps: Information emerges that may affect the officer's fitness and propriety
Verify the facts, using independent sources where the information is material
The board, nominations committee or delegated body reassesses and records its reasoning
If the officer is found not fit and proper, the officer ceases to act and the bank removes them
Notify BNM in writing, with reasons, within seven days of the cessation
Reallocate the officer's responsibilities and update the responsibility map

cards.title: Disqualified or not fit and proper?

items.label: Legal basis
items.right: FSA section 60 and the BNM policy document

items.label: How it works
items.right: Board judgement on all relevant factors

items.label: Examples
items.left: Undischarged bankruptcy; proven dishonesty or fraud charge
items.right: Poor integrity record; lack of competence; judgment debts

items.label: Consequence
items.left: Must cease; bank terminates without compensation
items.right: Must cease; bank removes from office

cards.back: Every director must commit to ongoing education and keep up with the business and market and regulatory developments (CG 9.2).
The board must give director development an adequate budget and keep up-to-date development plans for each director (CG 13.3).
Each year the board evaluates the board, its committees and individual directors to find development needs (CG 13.1).
BNM's guidance encourages the board to use external experts from time to time to make evaluations more objective (CG 13.2).
The board documents the skills it needs, individually and collectively, and reviews them as strategy and risks change (CG 11.2).
BNM's RMiT policy document also requires board members to take part in cybersecurity awareness and receive regular technology training.

cards.question: Selasih's new independent director has strong credit expertise but no technology experience. What does BNM expect?
options: Reject her, because every director must have every skill
Appoint her and leave technology issues to the technology committee
Explain the gap in the BNM application and set a development plan to close it
Appoint her only as an alternate director until she qualifies
cards.explanation: Appendix 3 asks the application to describe any skill gaps and how the board will support the candidate, and paragraph 13.3 requires development plans. Alternate directors are not allowed, and skills are judged for the board collectively.

cards.title: Verify, then document
cards.body:
- If you rely on information the person gave you and it matters to the decision, check it against independent sources (paragraph 10.2).
- Keep assessment records confidential and keep them for the period your policy sets.
- Keep the list of key responsible persons current; BNM can add people it thinks were missed.
- Record why a weak factor was or was not decisive. 'Board satisfied' with no reasons will not survive a supervisory review.

cards.title: Stage 2 take-aways
items: BNM must approve chairmen, directors and the CEO before appointment, and a bank must have a CEO at all times.
Section 59 disqualifications are automatic; fit and proper failures under section 60 are judgements on probity, competence and financial integrity.
Assess before appointment, at least annually, and whenever new material information appears, and verify key facts independently.
A disqualified or unfit person must cease to act at once, and BNM must be told within seven days with reasons.
Directors must commit to ongoing education, backed by a budget, development plans and annual evaluations.
Real case: weak succession planning left an insurer without an approved CEO for 16 months and cost RM336,000.

cards.prompt: If you were assessed tomorrow on competency for your own role, what evidence of training, skills and experience could you show? Where is the gap?

quiz.question: Under section 54 of the Financial Services Act 2013, which appointment at Selasih Bank needs BNM's prior written approval?
options: Hiring a new branch manager in Ipoh
Appointing a deputy to the head of internal audit
Reappointing an existing director for a new term
Promoting a relationship manager to team leader
quiz.explanation: Section 54(2) covers appointment and reappointment of the chairman, directors and CEO of a licensed person. Other senior officers must meet fit and proper requirements under section 55 but do not need prior approval under section 54.

quiz.question: Which event automatically disqualifies a person from being a senior officer of a bank under section 59(1)?
options: Having an unsatisfied judgment debt on a car loan
Being under internal investigation for a missed deadline
Being an undischarged bankrupt
Having been dismissed for poor sales performance
quiz.explanation: Section 59(1)(a) disqualifies an undischarged bankrupt. A judgment debt is a fit and proper factor under financial integrity, weighed with others, not an automatic bar.

quiz.question: Selasih's Chief Risk Officer resigns to join another bank. What must Selasih do under section 62?
options: Nothing, because the resignation is voluntary and not misconduct
Obtain BNM's approval before accepting the resignation
Notify BNM in writing of the cessation and its reasons within seven days
Notify BNM within thirty days, together with the name of the proposed successor
quiz.explanation: Section 62 applies to cessations 'under any other circumstances' too, so a voluntary resignation must be notified in writing with reasons within seven days.

quiz.question: How often, at a minimum, must Selasih reassess the fitness and propriety of its directors and senior officers?
options: At least annually, and also whenever material new information emerges
Only at appointment, unless BNM asks for a review
Every three years, aligned to the end of each director's term of office
Only when the person is promoted or changes role
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10.1 of the Fit and Proper Criteria policy document and paragraphs 10.8 and 17.6 of the Corporate Governance document require assessment before appointment, at least annually, and whenever information arises that may materially compromise fitness.

quiz.question: The board has delegated fit and proper decisions on senior officers to the CEO. A poor appointment is later criticised by BNM. Who remains accountable?
options: The board, because it remains accountable for delegated assessments and decisions
Only the CEO, because the assessment and the decision were formally delegated to him
Only the human resources department that prepared the file
Nobody, because delegation transfers accountability to a committee
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 8.3 says that where the board and nominations committee delegate senior officer assessments to the CEO or a committee, the board remains accountable for them.

quiz.question: A director candidate gives Selasih a CV saying he led a bank's risk function for five years. The claim is central to his appointment. What does the policy document require?
options: Accept the CV, because candidates sign a declaration that it is true
Ask the candidate for a second, more detailed CV
Take reasonable steps to verify the claim against independent sources
Leave verification to BNM, which checks every candidate when it reviews the application
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10.2 says that where significant reliance is placed on material information from the person being assessed, the institution must take reasonable steps to verify it independently.

quiz.question: Which statement about financial integrity is correct under BNM's Fit and Proper Criteria policy document?
options: A person must own property in Malaysia to pass the criterion
Any personal loan from another bank is a conflict of interest that fails the financial criterion
Financial integrity is assessed only for directors, not for senior officers
Having limited personal wealth does not in itself mean a person fails the criterion
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 13.3 states that limited financial means does not by itself affect the ability to meet the financial integrity criterion. The focus is on meeting obligations and unsatisfied judgment debts.

quiz.question: Which practice best meets paragraph 13.3 of the Corporate Governance policy document on director development?
options: An adequate budget plus a development plan for each director that is regularly updated
A single induction session for new directors on their first day
Allowing directors to attend any conference they choose each year, without a written plan or budget
Expecting directors to arrange and fund their own training
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 13.3 requires the board to dedicate sufficient resources, including an adequate budget and regularly updated development plans, so each director has the knowledge and skills needed.

quiz.question: In BNM's 2026 action against The Pacific Insurance Berhad, what did BNM identify as the cause of the breach?
options: A CEO who was found to be disqualified after appointment
Inadequate succession planning that delayed a CEO application for approval
Failure to notify BNM within seven days that the previous CEO had resigned from the company
Appointing a CEO before BNM's written approval had been granted
quiz.explanation: BNM's press release says the CEO post was vacant from November 2024 to March 2026 because inadequate succession planning meant a suitable candidate was not identified and submitted for approval in time.

quiz.question: Selasih's Head of Treasury is charged in court with a fraud offence. The case is pending. Which statement reflects section 59(2)?
options: He is already disqualified and must be dismissed without compensation
He may continue fully in his role until any conviction, since the charge has not yet been proven in court
Only BNM can decide whether he continues, without any board role
He must not act as Head of Treasury unless the board permits it, subject to conditions BNM specifies
quiz.explanation: Section 59(2) bars a person facing pending proceedings for a dishonesty or fraud offence from acting or taking part in the institution's affairs, except as permitted by the board subject to BNM's conditions. Disqualification under 59(1) needs a proven charge.

sessions.title: Responsibility Mapping: Who Owns What from 1 January 2026
sessions.summary: BNM's Responsibility Mapping policy document: the four principles, the CEO's allocation duty, conduct duties of senior managers, delegation and shared responsibilities, group functions, documentation and written acknowledgements.
objectives: Explain why BNM introduced responsibility mapping and how it sits alongside committees
Describe the board's and CEO's roles and the Appendix 1 responsibilities and Appendix 2 roles
Apply the rules on delegation, shared responsibilities and affiliate officers
Prepare documentation and acknowledgements that meet paragraphs 7.14 to 7.18

cards.title: Not me
cards.setting: Dry-run interview for the BNM review, meeting room 12B.

lines.text: Dry run. I'll play the BNM supervisor. Question one: who at Selasih is accountable for the controls that protect customer information?
Well... HR trains staff on secrecy, but the controls aren't mine.
Lee Jia Hui, Branch Operations, Johor Bahru. We follow the procedures, but we don't own the framework.
IT says it's the CISO, the CISO says data ownership sits with the business. That is exactly the blind spot BNM wrote this policy to remove.
Stage 3 then: Responsibility Mapping. By the end of today, every question like that should have one clear name as the answer.

scenes.heading: Gaps BNM saw
scenes.narration: BNM said it had observed gaps in the span of control of senior management, which raised risks from weak oversight of operations.

scenes.heading: The aim
scenes.narration: Every function, including duties set by law and by BNM's policy documents, must be clearly allocated to a named member of senior management with the competence and authority to deliver it.

scenes.heading: In force
scenes.narration: The policy document was issued on 29 December 2023 and took effect on 1 January 2026 for licensed banks and other institutions.

scenes.heading: Committees still work
scenes.narration: Responsibility mapping runs alongside collective decision-making in committees. It does not replace them; it makes individual accountability visible within them.

scenes.heading: Consequences inside the bank first
scenes.narration: BNM expects banks to apply their own consequences for misconduct by senior managers. Except for serious misconduct, BNM does not generally plan enforcement as an immediate response to individual poor behaviour.

cards.title: The four principles
cards.caption: Responsibility Mapping policy document, paragraph 7. All four principles are standards (S).

items.label: 1. Identify and allocate
items.detail: An effective process to find all responsibilities and assign each one to senior management, overseen by the board.

items.label: 2. Fit and proper owners
items.detail: The CEO allocates every responsibility to senior officers who are fit and proper and have real authority.

items.label: 3. Accountable conduct
items.detail: Owners are accountable for their areas and their staff, including when they delegate.

items.label: 4. Documented and current
items.detail: Complete, up-to-date documentation and a written acknowledgement from each senior manager.

cards.question: Who must make sure that all of Selasih's responsibilities are comprehensively identified and allocated to senior officers?
options: The board audit committee
The CEO, leading senior management, under the board's oversight
The Chief Compliance Officer, as owner of regulatory matters
Each department head, for their own team only
cards.explanation: Paragraphs 7.3 and 7.4 give the CEO responsibility for identifying responsibilities and allocating them to fit and proper senior officers. Paragraph 7.1 makes the board responsible for overseeing the framework.

cards.title: Senior management roles in Appendix 2
cards.prompt: Match each minimum senior management role to the primary responsibility the policy document describes.

pairs.right: The risk management function and the risk management framework.
Compliance with regulatory requirements and internal policies and procedures.
The technology risk management function.
HR policies, including recruitment, performance, remuneration and consequence management.
Assuring the adequacy and effectiveness of internal controls.
Managing and conducting a business activity such as retail or corporate banking or treasury.

cards.title: What an accountable senior manager must do
Who stays accountable?
cards.prompt: Decide whether the named senior manager still carries accountability in each case.

items.text: The CFO delegates monthly regulatory returns to a competent deputy
The CFO and CRO share responsibility for capital management and stress testing
A decision on her area was taken by the management credit committee she sits on
The COO left a temporary gap by handing over verbally to an untrained manager
Her responsibility was formally reallocated, documented and acknowledged by her successor
The board approved a reorganisation and the new owner signed an updated acknowledgement

cards.title: Real case: oversight gaps and group functions (BNM, 2024)
cards.body:
On 22 July 2024 BNM imposed an administrative monetary penalty of **RM88,000** on Bank of China (Malaysia) Berhad.

BNM's press release of 23 August 2024 says the bank relocated two core banking systems to new data centres in December 2022 and February 2023 without BNM's prior approval. BNM treated this as a significant modification of an approved material outsourcing arrangement, which needs written approval under the Outsourcing policy document.

BNM linked the breach to **gaps in the bank's oversight of its outsourcing activities** and its internal policies. The bank's fixes included periodic reviews of outsourcing arrangements and better coordination with the **group functions** that carry out material activities for it.

**Lesson for responsibility mapping:** when group or shared functions do work for a Malaysian bank, the Malaysian entity still needs a named senior manager who understands that work, controls it and makes sure local rules are met. Appendix 1 lists operational resilience, including outsourcing risk, as a responsibility that must be allocated.

cards.title: The regional CTO
cards.setting: Video call with the group technology office.

lines.text: Group wants their regional CTO, employed by a group technology company in another country, to own Selasih's technology operations responsibility. Is that allowed?
Only if his employer is supervised by BNM, or by a financial regulator that has an effective supervisory cooperation arrangement with BNM.
Our group technology company is not a financial institution and nobody supervises it as one.
Then he cannot be the allocated owner. And even where an affiliate's officer is allowed, our board and CEO must be able to influence his performance assessment and pay.

cards.title: Who should own technology operations?
cards.situation: Selasih's CEO must allocate responsibility for implementing information technology strategy and managing IT operations before the BNM review. Options on the table: the group's regional CTO (employed by an unsupervised group technology company); Selasih's own Head of IT, who has the authority and budget but has been in role for two months; or a joint arrangement. What should the CEO do?

choices.text: Allocate it to Selasih's Head of IT after due diligence on competence, document how the group company supports him, and record the arrangement in the responsibility map.
choices.outcome: Best. Paragraph 7.7 rules out an officer of an unsupervised affiliate, and paragraph 7.6 requires due diligence on competence and attention to where decision-making really sits. Documenting the group support makes the dependency visible.

choices.text: Allocate it to the regional CTO because he makes most technology decisions in practice.
choices.outcome: Real decision-making matters, but paragraph 7.7 only allows allocation to an affiliate's officer if the affiliate is supervised by BNM or by a regulator with an effective cooperation arrangement. Here it is not.

choices.text: Leave it unallocated until the Head of IT has more experience.
choices.outcome: Unallocated responsibilities are the blind spots the policy was written to prevent. Allocate it now and support the owner with development.

choices.text: Share it jointly between the Head of IT and the regional CTO.
choices.outcome: A shared responsibility makes both jointly and severally accountable, but the regional CTO is still not an eligible owner under paragraph 7.7. Better than nothing, but not compliant as designed.

cards.title: Is the allocation real?
cards.caption: Paragraph 7.6 asks the CEO to check competence, authority and capability, and where decisions are really made, not just job titles.

items.label: Capable owner, no power
items.detail: Fix authority, budget or reporting lines before relying on the allocation.

items.label: Right owner
items.detail: Competent and holds real decision authority. Document and acknowledge.

items.label: Blind spot
items.detail: Neither capability nor authority. Reallocate now.

items.label: Power without capability
items.detail: Develop quickly or reallocate; record the plan.

cards.title: Building Selasih's responsibility map
cards.prompt: Arrange the steps in a sensible order.
steps: Board confirms oversight of the responsibility mapping framework
CEO identifies all responsibilities, including Appendix 1 and Selasih's own
Due diligence on each candidate owner's competence, authority and capability
Allocate each responsibility to a senior officer and document it with the owner's involvement
Each senior manager gives a written acknowledgement of their responsibilities
Re-obtain acknowledgements when responsibilities change significantly, and keep records ready for BNM

cards.back: Someone other than the CEO, employed by the bank or an affiliate, with authority and responsibility for planning, directing or controlling the bank's activities.
Two senior managers co-lead one function; the documentation explains whether their responsibilities are the same or different.
One responsibility held by more than one senior manager; all are jointly and severally accountable.
Obtained at appointment and again after significant changes, so the bank's expectations and the manager's understanding match.
Performance, pay and discipline frameworks the board must align with the mapping framework.
The bank must make its documentation of responsibilities available to BNM when asked.

cards.question: Selasih's Chief Operating Officer delegates outsourcing oversight to a vendor management head. A material vendor failure follows. Under paragraph 7.11, what is the COO's position?
options: She is no longer accountable because the task was delegated in writing
She remains accountable and had to ensure the delegate was competent and overseen
Accountability passes to the board audit committee
Only the vendor is accountable under the outsourcing contract
cards.explanation: Delegation is allowed only to a competent and capable person, and the senior manager remains accountable for the responsibility and for its effective discharge.

cards.title: Writing a responsibility statement that works
cards.body:
- Use verbs and outcomes: 'ensures customer information controls are designed, operated and tested', not 'oversees data'.
- Name the decision forums the person sits in and what they decide there.
- Spell out shared responsibilities: who does what, and that both remain accountable.
- Include interim and project responsibilities with real deliverables.
- Draft it with the manager concerned, then get the written acknowledgement.

cards.title: Stage 3 take-aways
items: Responsibility Mapping took effect on 1 January 2026: every responsibility must be allocated to a named, fit and proper senior officer.
The board oversees the framework; the CEO identifies and allocates responsibilities after due diligence on competence and real authority.
Owners must act with integrity, care and diligence, take reasonable steps on control, compliance and delegation, and be open with BNM.
Delegation does not remove accountability, and shared responsibilities make each owner jointly and severally accountable.
Each senior manager acknowledges their responsibilities in writing at appointment and after significant changes; BNM can ask for the documents.
Group or shared functions do not remove the need for a local owner who understands and controls the work.

cards.prompt: Pick one process you work in. Can you name the senior manager accountable for it? If not, what question would you ask to find out?

quiz.question: From which date did BNM's Responsibility Mapping policy document take effect?
options: 29 December 2023
1 July 2024
3 August 2016
1 January 2026
quiz.explanation: The policy document was issued on 29 December 2023 and paragraph 4.1 sets 1 January 2026 as its effective date. 3 August 2016 is the Corporate Governance document's date.

quiz.question: What is the board's role under Principle 1 of Responsibility Mapping?
options: Allocate every responsibility personally to each senior officer
Sign each senior manager's written acknowledgement on their behalf
Oversee the adoption and implementation of the framework and be satisfied the process is effective
Approve the framework once when it is adopted, then leave all further review to the CEO and management
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7.1 makes the board responsible for overseeing the framework and being satisfied that responsibilities are identified, assigned, assessed for fitness and documented. Allocation is the CEO's job under paragraphs 7.3 and 7.4.

quiz.question: Selasih's CFO and CRO jointly hold the responsibility for capital management, including ICAAP and stress testing. A stress test proves badly flawed. Who is accountable?
options: Only the CFO, because capital belongs to finance
Both, jointly and severally
Only the CRO, because stress testing is a risk tool
Neither, because the decision was taken by a committee
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7.12 makes all individuals sharing a responsibility jointly and severally accountable. Committee decision-making exists in parallel and does not remove individual accountability.

quiz.question: When must a senior manager at Selasih give a written acknowledgement of their allocated responsibilities?
options: Only once, when the policy first took effect
Every month, as part of the senior management performance report to the board
Only when BNM asks for the documentation
At appointment, and again whenever their responsibilities change significantly
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7.17 requires the acknowledgement at the time of appointment at minimum, reviewed and re-obtained when there are significant changes to the responsibilities allocated.

quiz.question: When allocating a responsibility, the CEO notices the formal owner is the Head of Retail, but pricing decisions are actually made by the regional sales director. What does paragraph 7.6 require?
options: Follow the organisation chart, because formal job titles are what BNM's supervisors review
Split the responsibility so that each of them owns half of it
Move pricing decisions to the board so no single officer is accountable
Have regard to where decision-making authority really sits, not only to formal titles
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7.6(b) tells the CEO to consider where decision-making authority resides in practice, not only formal designation. The map should match reality or the reality should change.

quiz.question: Which of these is listed in Appendix 1 as a responsibility every bank must allocate to senior management?
options: Approval of the annual staff party budget
Selection of the bank's external lawyers
Integrity of all regulatory reporting
Design of the bank's logo and branding
quiz.explanation: Appendix 1 includes regulatory reporting integrity, along with risk management, recovery planning, customer information, operational resilience, fair treatment, capital and AML/CFT/CPF.

quiz.question: Selasih's group wants an officer employed by an unregulated group technology company abroad to own a Selasih responsibility. What does the policy document say?
options: Permitted, as long as the officer is employed within the same financial group as Selasih and reports to its CEO
Not allowed unless the affiliate is supervised by BNM or by a regulator cooperating effectively with BNM
Permitted, if the officer agrees to visit Malaysia every quarter
Permitted, if the Malaysian CEO signs a written guarantee of performance
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7.7 allows allocation to an affiliate's officer only where the affiliate is a BNM-supervised institution or is supervised by a financial regulator with an effective cooperation arrangement with BNM.

quiz.question: Which statement about BNM's approach to individual misconduct under Responsibility Mapping is accurate?
options: BNM will fine every senior manager personally whenever any breach occurs in their area, however minor or technical
BNM expects banks to apply consequences themselves and generally reserves immediate enforcement for serious misconduct
BNM will not act against misconduct, because accountability is purely internal
Banks may ignore minor misconduct as long as it is recorded in the map
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 1.7 says BNM looks to institutions to make sure misconduct meets appropriate consequences and, except in serious cases, does not generally expect immediate enforcement against individual poor behaviour.

quiz.question: What did BNM link to Bank of China (Malaysia) Berhad's 2024 penalty for relocating core banking systems without approval?
options: Gaps in its oversight of outsourcing activities and related internal policies
A cyber attack that destroyed its primary data centre and its backup systems in 2023
Failure to submit suspicious transaction reports on time
A director who failed to disclose a conflict of interest
quiz.explanation: BNM's press release attributes the non-compliance to gaps in the bank's oversight of outsourcing and its related policies, and notes improved coordination with group functions as part of the remedy.

quiz.question: Selasih's documentation for the Chief Operating Officer describes only her job title and reporting line. What is missing under paragraph 7.16?
options: Her salary, bonus and personal contact details
Her regulatory, interim, shared and committee responsibilities, and how shared ones are split
A copy of every procedure manual in her division
BNM's written approval of the documentation before each senior manager's responsibilities take effect
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7.16 lists what the documentation must contain, including regulatory responsibilities such as Appendix 1 items, interim or project duties, shared roles and responsibilities, and responsibilities in collective forums. BNM receives it on request but does not pre-approve it.

sessions.title: Speaking Up: Code of Ethics, Whistleblowing Channels and Protection
sessions.summary: The code of ethics and whistleblowing policy BNM requires, the internal and external channels including BNM's own, who must be told about them, how protection works and how to spot and stop reprisal.
objectives: Describe the code of ethics and whistleblowing requirements in paragraph 18 of the Corporate Governance policy document
Choose between whistleblowing, grievance and complaint routes
Explain how BNM's whistleblowing channel and the Whistleblower Protection Act 2010 protect good-faith reporters
Recognise and respond to reprisal against a whistleblower

cards.title: Numbers that don't add up
cards.setting: Johor Bahru regional office, after hours.

lines.text: Haslina, can I ask something off the record? Our regional head told branch managers to move complaints logged in the last week of the quarter into next quarter, so our numbers look better for head office.
That is a question about integrity in reporting, and it is exactly what our whistleblowing policy is for.
He decides my bonus. If he finds out it was me, I'm finished in this region.
BNM requires us to let people raise concerns in confidence and without risk of reprisal. Let's look at your options together.
Stage 4: speaking up. The code of ethics, the whistleblowing policy, the channels inside and outside the bank, and what protection really means.

cards.title: What BNM requires on culture and speaking up

scenes.heading: A code of ethics
scenes.narration: Paragraph 18.1 of the Corporate Governance policy document requires a code of ethics covering confidentiality, conflicts of interest, integrity in reporting and fair treatment of customers. Breaches must be recorded and dealt with.

scenes.heading: A whistleblowing policy
scenes.narration: Paragraph 18.2 requires a whistleblowing policy so that concerns about illegal, unethical or questionable practices are objectively investigated and addressed.

scenes.heading: Confidence, no reprisal
scenes.narration: People must be able to raise concerns in confidence and without the risk of reprisal.

scenes.heading: Clear routes
scenes.narration: The policy must name who inside the bank receives concerns, and people must be made aware of other avenues to regulators and law enforcement.

scenes.heading: Beyond employees
scenes.narration: The policy must reach contractors, consultants and interns, and let them report. A non-executive director is designated to make sure it works.

cards.title: How a concern travels inside Selasih
cards.caption: Paragraph 18.2 and its footnote: the designated director evaluates periodic reports on how concerns are escalated and handled, and oversees reviews of the policy.

items.label: Concern raised
items.detail: Through the named internal channels, in writing where possible, with facts and documents.

items.label: Logged confidentially
items.detail: The reporter's identity is shared only with those who must know.

items.label: Objective investigation
items.detail: By people independent of the area and of anyone implicated.

items.label: Action and feedback
items.detail: Breaches addressed promptly; the reporter is told the outcome where possible.

items.label: Board oversight
items.detail: The designated non-executive director reviews periodic reports and the policy's effectiveness.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT one of the four specific things paragraph 18.2 requires a bank to do?
options: Name the parties within the bank to whom concerns can be escalated
Make individuals aware of avenues to regulators or law enforcement
Require every whistleblower to give their name before a report is accepted
Designate a non-executive director responsible for effective implementation
cards.explanation: Paragraph 18.2 lists internal escalation points, awareness of external avenues, communication to third parties such as contractors, consultants and interns, and a designated non-executive director. It does not require reporters to identify themselves.

cards.title: Which route fits?
cards.prompt: Sort each situation into the channel that fits it best.

items.text: A regional head orders complaints to be shifted between quarters to flatter results
An employee disagrees with her performance rating
A customer says a fee was charged that the product sheet did not mention
A procurement officer appears to steer contracts to a relative's firm
A staff member wants a transfer to be closer to family
A contractor sees a manager sharing customer files with an outside party
A customer is unhappy with how long a loan approval took

cards.title: Outside the bank: reporting to BNM
cards.body:
BNM's whistleblowing policy page explains its own channel:

- BNM accepts disclosures of **improper conduct**, including any person's failure to comply with the laws BNM administers, such as the Financial Services Act. Reports about a **financial institution and its staff** go to BNM's designated persons through the form on that page.
- A whistleblower who discloses in **good faith** is protected under the **Whistleblower Protection Act 2010**: confidentiality, immunity from civil and criminal liability for the disclosure, and protection from detrimental action.
- Protection can be **revoked or excluded**, for example if the disclosure is frivolous or known to be false, made mainly to avoid dismissal, or if the whistleblower took part in the misconduct.
- **Anonymous** reporters are not given whistleblower protection, and BNM can only investigate what the report contains.
- Knowingly false disclosures are a criminal offence.
- Ordinary product or service complaints go to **BNMLINK**, not the whistleblowing channel.

Your bank's policy must make staff aware of routes like this.

lines.text: If I report anonymously inside the bank, nobody can retaliate. Isn't that safest?
Our internal channel accepts anonymous reports, and you can choose that. But investigators can't come back to you with questions, and the facts may be harder to prove.
If you give your name, the policy limits who knows it. Retaliation against you would itself be misconduct we would act on.
And if you ever go to BNM instead, remember its page says anonymous reporters don't get protection under the Whistleblower Protection Act.
Then I'll report with my name, in writing, with the complaint log extracts. And I'll note who I've told.

cards.title: He found out
cards.situation: Two weeks after Jia Hui's report, the regional head learns who made it. He tells HR he wants to transfer her to a small branch three hours away 'for operational reasons' and cut her role in the regional sales review. The investigation into the complaint logs has not finished. You are in Amirul's HR team. What do you do?

choices.text: Put the transfer on hold, escalate to the whistleblowing investigation lead and the designated non-executive director, and treat the move as possible reprisal to be investigated.
choices.outcome: Best. BNM requires that people can raise concerns without risk of reprisal. A move that follows a report, ordered by the person reported on, must be stopped and looked at independently, and the board's designated director should know.

choices.text: Process the transfer, because regional heads decide postings in their region.
choices.outcome: This lets the person under investigation punish the reporter. It undermines the policy and would discourage anyone else from speaking up.

choices.text: Ask Jia Hui whether she minds the transfer, and process it if she agrees.
choices.outcome: Asking her is kind, but she is under pressure from the person she reported. The timing and source of the request still need independent review first.

choices.text: Tell the regional head that HR cannot discuss the report, and approve a shorter-distance transfer instead.
choices.outcome: A smaller detriment is still a detriment. The issue is not distance but whether the move is retaliation.

cards.title: Inside the bank or to BNM?
cards.caption: Bank staff can use either. A good internal channel is usually the fastest way to stop harm, but the external route must stay open.

items.label: Who receives it
items.left: Named internal recipients set in the bank's policy
items.right: BNM's designated persons, using BNM's form

items.label: Typical matters
items.left: Breaches of law, the code of ethics or internal policy
items.right: Improper conduct, including breaches of laws BNM administers

items.label: Protection
items.left: The bank must protect against reprisal
items.right: Whistleblower Protection Act 2010, for good-faith reports

items.label: Oversight and feedback
items.right: BNM's designated person tells the reporter the outcome

cards.front: Myth: only employees can use it
cards.back: Fact: the policy must be communicated to contractors, consultants and interns, and they must be able to report.
Fact: you need an honest, reasonable concern and the facts you have. Investigation is the bank's job.

cards.front: Myth: it's the same as a grievance
cards.back: Fact: grievances are about your own treatment. Whistleblowing is about wrongdoing that affects the bank, customers or the public.

cards.front: Myth: going to BNM is disloyal
cards.back: Fact: BNM requires banks to make staff aware of external avenues to regulators and law enforcement.

cards.front: Myth: a false report costs nothing
cards.back: Fact: knowingly false disclosures lose protection and can be a criminal offence.
Fact: the designated director oversees periodic reviews of whether the policy actually works.

cards.title: Who does what in Selasih's speak-up framework
cards.prompt: Match each part of the framework to its role.

pairs.right: Responsible for effective implementation; reviews reports on how concerns are handled.
Covers confidentiality, conflicts of interest, integrity in reporting and fair treatment; breaches are recorded.
Deals with actual or suspected breaches promptly and keeps the board informed.
Gives anyone an avenue to disclose information relevant to assessing key responsible persons, with protection.
Handles general enquiries and complaints about products and services, not whistleblowing.

cards.question: A contractor working on Selasih's core banking upgrade sees a manager approve invoices for work that was never done. What does BNM's Corporate Governance policy document expect?
options: Nothing, because contractors are outside the bank's whistleblowing policy
The contractor should have been told about the policy and must be able to report the concern
The contractor must report only to the vendor's own management
The contractor must first get permission from the manager concerned
cards.explanation: Paragraph 18.2(c) requires the policy to be communicated to third parties such as contractors, consultants and interns, and to allow them to report concerns.

cards.title: Example: a report handled well
cards.body:
Selasih's investigation into the Johor Bahru complaint logs (the quest's own story) followed the policy:

- The case went to an investigator from Internal Audit, outside the region's reporting line.
- Only the investigator, the Chief Compliance Officer and the designated director knew the reporter's name.
- The transfer request against Jia Hui was frozen within a day and later withdrawn.
- The logs showed 63 complaints moved between quarters. The regional head received a final written warning, his variable pay was adjusted, and the complaints data sent to the board was restated.
- The code of ethics breach register was updated, and the designated director reported the case, anonymised, to the board.

Notice the links: integrity in reporting (code of ethics), protection from reprisal (whistleblowing policy), consequence management (Responsibility Mapping and remuneration rules) and honest information to the board.

cards.title: Raising a concern so it can be acted on
cards.body:
- Put it in writing if you can.
- Say **what** happened, **who** was involved, and **how, when and where**, and attach documents you are allowed to hold.
- Give your name if you can; it lets investigators ask follow-up questions.
- Stick to facts, not conclusions.
- Don't investigate on your own or tip off the people involved.
- Keep a note of who you reported to and when.

cards.title: Stage 4 take-aways
items: BNM requires a code of ethics covering confidentiality, conflicts, integrity in reporting and fair treatment, with breaches recorded and addressed.
The whistleblowing policy must allow confidential reporting without reprisal and objective investigation of concerns.
It must name internal recipients, make people aware of external avenues, reach contractors, consultants and interns, and have a designated non-executive director.
BNM accepts disclosures about financial institutions and their staff; good-faith reporters get Whistleblower Protection Act protection, but anonymous ones do not.
Retaliation against a reporter is itself serious misconduct and must be stopped and investigated.

cards.prompt: Do you know the names or channels you would use to raise a concern at your bank today, and the external route? If not, where would you look first?

quiz.question: Which topics must a bank's code of ethics address under paragraph 18.1 of BNM's Corporate Governance policy document?
options: Confidentiality, conflicts of interest, integrity in reporting and fair treatment of customers
Dress code, working hours, leave entitlements, travel claims and the proper use of office equipment
Marketing targets, branch opening hours and product pricing
Only conflicts of interest, since other topics are covered by law
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 18.1 requires the code to address confidentiality, conflicts of interest, integrity in reporting and fair treatment of customers, and the bank must keep a record of breaches.

quiz.question: Who must Selasih designate to be responsible for the effective implementation of its whistleblowing policy?
options: The Chief Executive Officer
The Chief Human Resource Officer
The head of the branch network
A non-executive director
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 18.2(d) requires a non-executive director to be designated. Its footnote adds that this includes reviewing periodic reports on how concerns are handled and overseeing reviews of the policy's effectiveness.

quiz.question: Selasih's whistleblowing policy is published only on the staff intranet, which contractors cannot access. Which requirement does this gap breach?
options: Communicating the policy to third parties such as contractors, consultants and interns and letting them report
Keeping a register of all breaches of the code of ethics and reporting it each quarter to the board audit committee
Disclosing the policy in the annual report of a listed bank
Obtaining BNM's prior approval of the policy text
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 18.2(c) requires the policy to be communicated to third parties such as contractors, consultants and interns, who must be allowed to report. BNM does not pre-approve the policy.

quiz.question: An employee wants to report directly to BNM that her bank is breaching the Financial Services Act. According to BNM's whistleblowing policy page, which statement is correct?
options: BNM only accepts disclosures about its own staff, so she must use the bank's channel
She must first exhaust the bank's internal whistleblowing channel and wait for its outcome before BNM will accept the report
BNM accepts such disclosures, and a good-faith whistleblower is protected under the Whistleblower Protection Act 2010
BNM accepts the report only if she remains anonymous
quiz.explanation: BNM's page lists failure by any person to comply with laws it administers as improper conduct it accepts, routes reports on financial institutions and their staff to designated persons, and gives good-faith whistleblowers WPA protections.

quiz.question: According to BNM's whistleblowing policy page, what happens to a person who reports improper conduct to BNM anonymously?
options: They receive exactly the same statutory protection as whistleblowers who give their names to BNM
The report is rejected and not investigated
BNM must trace and identify them before acting
No whistleblower protection is given, and BNM can investigate only what the report contains
quiz.explanation: BNM states that anonymous reporters are not accorded whistleblower protection and that its ability to investigate is limited to the contents of the report.

quiz.question: Which disclosure would lose protection under the exclusions BNM describes?
options: A report made in good faith that later turns out not to show a breach
A report made mainly to avoid a disciplinary action the employee is already facing
A report backed by documents the employee lawfully holds and has kept since the events
A report made by a contractor rather than an employee
quiz.explanation: BNM's page lists exclusions including disclosures made solely or substantially to avoid dismissal or disciplinary action, frivolous or knowingly false reports, and participation in the misconduct. Good faith matters, not whether the concern is ultimately proven.

quiz.question: A customer tells a branch officer that a fee was charged that the product disclosure sheet did not mention. Which route is most appropriate?
options: The whistleblowing channel, since an undisclosed fee may breach BNM's disclosure rules
The designated non-executive director, directly
The bank's complaints handling process, with BNMLINK available for the customer
A police report, since an unexplained fee may be fraud
quiz.explanation: A product or service complaint by a customer goes through complaints handling. BNM's page directs general enquiries and product complaints to BNMLINK, not to whistleblowing. If staff see a pattern of wrongdoing behind it, that could separately be a whistleblowing matter.

quiz.question: After an employee reports a regional head, the regional head asks HR to transfer her to a remote branch. What is the best response?
options: Approve it if the regional head confirms it is for operational reasons
Halt the transfer and have its link to the report reviewed independently, informing the investigation lead
Approve it but give the employee a pay rise to compensate
Ask the regional head to wait until the investigation has ended, and then approve the transfer if still needed
quiz.explanation: BNM requires that concerns can be raised without risk of reprisal. A move requested by the person under investigation must be stopped and examined independently; delaying it until after the investigation does not remove the reprisal risk.

quiz.question: Which statement best describes the link between Selasih's fit and proper policy and speaking up?
options: It must let anyone in the bank disclose information relevant to assessing key responsible persons, with protection
It must allow only directors to comment on each other's fitness and propriety
It replaces the whistleblowing policy for every concern raised about the conduct of directors and senior management
It requires staff to report every personal debt of a senior officer to BNM
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 9.1(iv) of the Fit and Proper Criteria policy document requires internal policies to provide avenues for any person in the institution to disclose relevant information, with protection from discriminatory action.

quiz.question: Why does BNM require banks to make staff aware of external whistleblowing avenues even when the internal channel works well?
options: So that staff send every concern to BNM first, rather than raising it through the bank's own internal channels
So concerns can still reach regulators or law enforcement if internal routes fail or are compromised
Because internal investigations are not allowed for regulatory breaches
Because BNM must approve the outcome of every internal investigation
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 18.2(b) requires awareness of other avenues to regulators or law enforcement. The internal channel remains the bank's main tool; the external route is a safeguard, not a replacement.

sessions.title: Respect at Work and Readiness: Harassment Duties, Enforcement and the Review
