sessions.summary: Sexual harassment duties under Part XVA of the Employment Act and the Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022, how BNM enforces and sets penalties, and how to show supervisors that governance works in practice.
objectives: Apply the Employment Act duties to inquire, give reasons for refusal and display the awareness notice
Explain the Tribunal route under the Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022
Describe BNM's enforcement actions, penalty factors, appeals and publication
Assemble the evidence a BNM governance review is likely to ask for

cards.title: A complaint from an intern
cards.setting: HR office, Selasih Bank head office, Kuala Lumpur.

lines.text: Final stage, and it starts with something serious. An intern in Treasury has complained in writing that a senior officer keeps making sexual remarks about her and touched her shoulder after she asked him to stop.
Then the Employment Act applies. We must inquire into the complaint, and we cannot simply decide not to without telling her why in writing.
He is also a key responsible person on our responsibility map. This touches his fitness and propriety too.
And the intern is exactly the kind of person our whistleblowing policy must reach. If she doesn't trust us, she can go elsewhere.
Stage 5: respect at work, how BNM enforces, and getting ready for the review. Then the final boss.

cards.title: Sexual harassment duties under the Employment Act 1955

scenes.heading: What it means
scenes.narration: The Act defines sexual harassment as unwanted conduct of a sexual nature, verbal, non-verbal, visual, gestural or physical, directed at a person, which is offensive, humiliating or a threat to their well-being, arising out of employment.

scenes.heading: Duty to inquire
scenes.narration: When an employer receives a complaint, it must inquire into it in the manner the Minister prescribes. Complaints can be by an employee against an employee, by an employee against the employer, or by the employer against an employee.

scenes.heading: Refusing is limited
scenes.narration: An employer may refuse only if the matter was already inquired into with no harassment proven, or the complaint is frivolous, vexatious or not in good faith. It must give written reasons within 30 days, and the complainant can refer the refusal to the Director General of Labour.

scenes.heading: If proven
scenes.narration: If the inquiry finds harassment by an employee, the employer must take disciplinary action, which can include dismissal without notice or downgrading.

scenes.heading: The notice
scenes.narration: Since 1 January 2023, section 81H requires every employer to display, at all times and in a conspicuous place, a notice raising awareness of sexual harassment.

cards.title: A complaint under Part XVA
cards.caption: Failing to inquire, to give written reasons for a refusal, or to report to the Director General when directed is an offence, with a fine of up to RM50,000 (section 81F).

items.label: Complaint received
items.detail: From an employee about a colleague or the employer, or by the employer about an employee.

items.label: Decide to inquire
items.detail: Inquire as prescribed; refuse only on the narrow grounds, with written reasons within 30 days.

items.label: Inquiry
items.detail: Fair, confidential and documented, with protection for the complainant.

items.label: Outcome
items.detail: If proven against an employee: disciplinary action up to dismissal without notice.

items.label: Director General
items.detail: Can direct an inquiry; the employer then reports back within 30 days.

cards.question: Selasih receives a sexual harassment complaint but decides the matter does not need an inquiry because the complaint is not in good faith. What must it do?
options: Nothing further, because the decision is HR's to make
Inform the complainant in writing of the refusal and the reasons within 30 days
Report the complaint to BNM within seven days
Ask the alleged harasser to confirm the complaint is not in good faith
cards.explanation: Section 81B(2) requires written notice of the refusal and the reasons as soon as practicable and within 30 days of receiving the complaint. The complainant can then refer the matter to the Director General.

cards.title: Could it be sexual harassment?
cards.prompt: Decide which situations could fall within the Employment Act's definition if they arise in the course of employment.

items.text: Repeated comments about a colleague's body after she asked him to stop
Sexual jokes and images posted in a team chat that a colleague finds humiliating
Suggestive gestures towards a colleague during a meeting
Unwanted touching by a manager at a team dinner
Firm, private feedback from a manager on poor-quality work
A dispute between two colleagues about who owns a project
A manager who shouts at staff when targets are missed

cards.title: The Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022
cards.body:
Alongside the Employment Act, the **Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022** (Act 840) gives anyone a separate route to redress. It comes into operation on dates the Minister appoints by notification.

- It sets up a **Tribunal for Anti-Sexual Harassment**. Any person may lodge a complaint about sexual harassment occurring after the Act came into operation.
- Its definition is close to the Employment Act's, but it is not limited to employment.
- The Tribunal decides on the **balance of probabilities**. Each panel has three members and must include at least one woman.
- It can order an apology (published, if the harassment was public), **compensation or damages of up to RM250,000**, or attendance at a programme. Failing to comply with an award is an offence.
- A complaint to the Tribunal does not stop anyone making a **police report** for an offence related to sexual harassment.
- An **Administrator** promotes prevention and awareness, including by asking people to display notices.

So a complainant can take the matter outside the bank, whatever the inquiry finds.

lines.text: The Treasurer just called me. He wants HR to 'have a quiet word' with the officer and move the intern to another team. No inquiry, no file.
That would breach section 81B and our own policy. Moving the complainant instead of dealing with the complaint is the opposite of protection.
There's also a governance angle. The officer is a key responsible person. New information that may affect his fitness and propriety triggers a reassessment.
And the Treasurer is the accountable senior manager for that area. Under responsibility mapping, he answers for conduct in his team, including how this is handled.

cards.title: What Selasih should do now
cards.situation: The written complaint is on file. The officer denies everything. The intern is anxious and asks not to sit near him. The Treasurer wants it settled informally. As the HR case lead, what is your plan?

choices.text: Open a formal inquiry, separate the two at work without disadvantaging the intern, keep it confidential, trigger a fit and proper reassessment of the officer, and record each step.
choices.outcome: Best. It meets the duty to inquire, protects the complainant, links the outcome to the fit and proper process, and leaves an audit trail BNM and the Director General can follow.

choices.text: Hold an informal mediation between them first, and start an inquiry only if mediation fails.
choices.outcome: Some workplaces offer informal options, but a written complaint triggers the duty to inquire. Pressing an anxious complainant into mediation with the accused can also harm her.

choices.text: Move the intern to another floor and close the file, as the Treasurer suggests.
choices.outcome: This is no inquiry at all and penalises the complainant. It risks an offence under section 81F and would destroy trust in the bank's speak-up channels.

choices.text: Suspend the officer without pay until the case ends, however long it takes.
choices.outcome: Protective steps may be needed, but punishment comes after a finding. Even then, the Act caps suspension without wages as a punishment at two weeks.

items.label: FSA in force; Fit and Proper Criteria effective
items.detail: Approvals, disqualification and the three fit and proper criteria.

items.label: Corporate Governance policy document
items.detail: Board, senior management, culture, whistleblowing and disclosures.

items.label: Sexual harassment notice duty
items.detail: Section 81H: awareness notice displayed at the workplace at all times.

items.label: Responsibility Mapping issued
items.detail: Two years' lead time to build the map.

items.label: Responsibility Mapping in force
items.detail: Every responsibility allocated and acknowledged.

items.detail: RM336,000 on The Pacific Insurance Berhad for weak succession planning.

cards.title: BNM's enforcement toolkit
cards.prompt: Match each enforcement action in BNM's Enforcement Approach to its description.

pairs.right: A monetary penalty BNM imposes itself, for example under section 234 of the FSA.
A monetary settlement offered with the consent of the Public Prosecutor.
An order to fix the breach and, where relevant, pay those who suffered losses.
A formal censure of the wrongdoer.
Charges in court for offences under the laws BNM administers.

cards.title: How BNM takes an enforcement decision
cards.prompt: Put the stages of BNM's published enforcement process in order.
steps: Breach detected, for example through supervision, complaints, media reports or self-reporting
BNM's department gathers evidence, establishes facts and recommends action
The Enforcement Committee decides the action and any penalty under its framework
BNM communicates its decision and gives a chance to make written representations
An appeal against a monetary penalty may go to the Monetary Penalty Review Committee within 21 days
BNM publishes the enforcement action on its website

cards.title: What BNM weighs when setting a penalty

cards.back: Was the breach deliberate, and how much care did the institution take?
Did it have reasonable controls in place for the area that failed?
Any similar or other breaches in the past five years?
Did it cooperate, report the breach voluntarily and fix it effectively?
Did the breach bring a gain or avoid a loss, and how much?
Since 2019 BNM publishes its enforcement actions, with facts and the factors it weighed.

cards.question: Which behaviour after a breach is most likely to count in Selasih's favour in BNM's penalty assessment?
options: Waiting for BNM to discover the breach during its next onsite review
Reporting the breach to BNM voluntarily and fixing it effectively
Disputing the facts until BNM produces every document
Paying a penalty early without changing the underlying process
cards.explanation: BNM's Enforcement Approach lists cooperation, voluntary reporting and effective remediation as post-misconduct factors. Paying early without fixing the cause does not address the breach.

cards.title: Getting ready for the governance review
cards.body:
- Check that the corporate governance disclosure, board charter and board composition details are on the website and up to date.
- Have the responsibility map, written acknowledgements and fit and proper records ready for BNM on request.
- Pull whistleblowing statistics and the designated director's reviews.
- Confirm the sexual harassment notice is displayed at every workplace and the complaints procedure is current.
- Rehearse: can each senior manager explain what they own and how they control it?

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways
items: Employers must inquire into sexual harassment complaints, refuse only on narrow grounds with written reasons within 30 days, and act on proven findings.
Since 1 January 2023 every employer must display a sexual harassment awareness notice at the workplace at all times.
The Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022 offers a Tribunal route, with compensation of up to RM250,000, alongside police reports.
Harassment by a key responsible person also raises fit and proper and responsibility mapping questions.
BNM can impose monetary penalties, compounds, reprimands and other actions, weighing culpability, controls, history and post-breach behaviour, and publishes them.
Readiness means documents that match reality: disclosures, maps, acknowledgements, assessments and speak-up records.

cards.prompt: Where is the sexual harassment notice displayed in your workplace, and would a new intern know how to raise a complaint safely? What would you improve?

quiz.question: Under section 81H of the Employment Act 1955, what must every employer do?
options: Run sexual harassment training for every employee once a year and keep attendance records for inspection
Display a notice raising awareness of sexual harassment conspicuously at the workplace at all times
Appoint a sexual harassment officer registered with the Director General
Report every sexual harassment complaint to the police within seven days
quiz.explanation: Section 81H, in force since 1 January 2023, requires the awareness notice. The Act does not itself set an annual training course or a duty to report every complaint to the police.

quiz.question: On what grounds may an employer refuse to inquire into a sexual harassment complaint under section 81B?
options: The person complained about is a senior manager with a strong record and no previous complaints against him in the bank
The complainant is an intern rather than a permanent employee
The alleged conduct happened at an after-work team dinner
It was already inquired into with no harassment proven, or it is frivolous, vexatious or not in good faith
quiz.explanation: Section 81B(3) allows refusal only on those two grounds, and section 81B(2) requires written reasons within 30 days. Seniority or the complainant's status are not grounds.

quiz.question: Selasih's inquiry finds that a branch officer sexually harassed a colleague. Which outcome does section 81C allow?
options: Only a written warning for a first offence
Suspension without wages for up to three months, followed by a final written warning on file
Dismissal without notice, downgrading, or a lesser punishment the employer thinks just
Referral to BNM, which then decides the punishment
quiz.explanation: Section 81C lets the employer dismiss without notice, downgrade or impose a lesser punishment, and caps suspension without wages at two weeks.

quiz.question: What is the maximum fine for an employer that fails to inquire into a sexual harassment complaint as required?
options: RM1 million
quiz.explanation: Section 81F, as amended with effect from 1 January 2023, sets a fine of up to RM50,000. RM250,000 is the Tribunal's compensation limit under the Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022.

quiz.question: Which statement about the Tribunal for Anti-Sexual Harassment is correct?
options: It decides complaints on the balance of probabilities and can award compensation of up to RM250,000
It hears only complaints that an employer has already refused to inquire into under the Employment Act
It decides complaints beyond reasonable doubt, like a criminal court
Lodging a complaint there bars the complainant from making a police report
quiz.explanation: Act 840 sets the balance of probabilities standard, allows compensation of up to RM250,000, and preserves the right to make a police report. Any person may lodge a complaint; it is not limited to refused workplace cases.

quiz.question: A senior officer on Selasih's responsibility map is the subject of a credible harassment complaint. Besides the Employment Act inquiry, what governance step is needed?
options: Nothing, since harassment is purely an HR matter
Remove him immediately as automatically disqualified under section 59
Ask BNM to run the harassment inquiry, since the officer is a key responsible person
Reassess his fitness and propriety, because material new information has emerged
quiz.explanation: Fit and proper assessments must be repeated when information arises that may materially compromise a person's fitness and propriety. A complaint is not a section 59 disqualification, and the inquiry is the employer's duty.

quiz.question: Which statement describes the Monetary Penalty Review Committee in BNM's Enforcement Approach?
options: BNM's internal committee of Deputy and Assistant Governors that decides all enforcement actions and penalties
An independent committee that hears appeals against BNM's monetary penalties, filed within 21 days
A court that hears criminal charges under the FSA
A board committee that every bank must set up to review fines
quiz.explanation: The MPRC is established under section 238 of the FSA to consider appeals against administrative monetary penalties or pecuniary remedies, and appeals must be filed within 21 days. Decisions on actions are taken by BNM's Enforcement Committee.

quiz.question: Which factor would BNM treat as aggravating when setting a penalty under its Enforcement and Penalty Framework?
options: Voluntary self-reporting of the breach to BNM before any supervisory review
A similar breach by the same institution within the past five years
Effective remediation completed before BNM's decision
Full cooperation during BNM's assessment
quiz.explanation: BNM considers history of past misconduct in the previous five years. Self-reporting, cooperation and effective remediation are behaviours after misconduct that can mitigate.

quiz.question: Where must Selasih publish its articles of association, board charter and up-to-date board composition?
options: Only in a confidential filing to BNM
On its website
Only in the notice of its annual general meeting
On the Companies Commission's portal
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 22.7 of the Corporate Governance policy document requires these to be published on the institution's website; paragraph 22.6 adds that the corporate governance disclosures are published there too.

quiz.question: A Selasih manager says the Employment Act's sexual harassment Part does not protect higher-paid staff earning above RM4,000 a month. Is he right?
options: No; the wage limit in the First Schedule switches off only some other provisions, so Part XVA covers all employees
Yes; Part XVA applies only to employees earning RM4,000 a month or less
Yes; staff earning above RM4,000 must use the Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022 Tribunal instead of the Employment Act
No; but only because banks are covered by BNM's rules instead of the Act
quiz.explanation: The First Schedule covers any person under a contract of service and, for those earning above RM4,000, disapplies only a short list of provisions on overtime, rest-day and holiday pay and termination benefits. Part XVA is not among them.

regulators: Tribunal for Anti-Sexual Harassment (Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022)

references.provision: Paragraphs 8 to 14, 16 to 18, 22 and Appendices 1 and 3
references.note: Board duties, director commitment and ongoing education, composition and independence, committees, evaluations and development budgets, conflicts, senior management, code of ethics and the whistleblowing policy.

references.title: Policy Document on Fit and Proper Criteria

references.note: Creates the Tribunal for Anti-Sexual Harassment, open to any person, deciding on the balance of probabilities with awards of up to RM250,000, without barring police reports.

references.note: Describes BNM's enforcement process, the actions available, aggravating and mitigating factors, appeals to the Monetary Penalty Review Committee and publication of actions.

references.title: Policy Document on Risk Management in Technology (RMiT)
references.note: The board must take part in cybersecurity awareness and training and receive regular training on technology developments.

bank.question: Selasih's board approves a high-growth unsecured lending plan that management proposed, with no change, in a 15-minute item. Months later losses mount. Which statement best reflects how BNM would view the board's role?
options: The board met its duty by approving a plan that competent and experienced management had prepared, tested and presented
Only management is answerable, because lending is a day-to-day matter
BNM expects evidence that the board challenged management on key strategic decisions, and the record shows none
The board is answerable only if a director personally benefited from the plan
bank.explanation: The Corporate Governance document says the board should have the competence and objectivity to challenge management and that BNM expects evidence of effective challenge on key strategic decisions. Section 56 also makes the board oversee strategy and senior management.

bank.question: A director of Selasih uses his board seat to push the bank to grant a loan that helps a friend's company, though the loan is commercially weak. Which section 57 duty is most directly engaged, and why does it matter?
options: The duty of care only; it is a civil matter for the bank's shareholders
The duty to attend 75% of meetings; it is enforced by the nominations committee
The duty to disclose interests; it applies only if he owns shares in the borrower
Using powers only for their proper purpose; breaching that limb is a criminal offence under the section
bank.explanation: Section 57(1)(c) requires powers to be used only for the purposes for which they were conferred, and section 57(3) makes a breach of that paragraph an offence. Good faith and independent judgement are also engaged.

bank.question: Selasih's board has nine members: the chairman (non-executive, non-independent), the CEO, one other executive director and six independent directors. What is the governance problem?
options: Six independent directors out of nine is not a majority of the board as BNM requires
The chairman must always be an independent director
The CEO is not permitted to sit on the board at all
Two executive directors sit on the board, which needs BNM's written approval
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.4 limits the board to one executive director unless BNM approves otherwise in writing. Six of nine is a majority, and a non-independent, non-executive chairman is allowed if he was not CEO in the past five years.

bank.question: An independent director of Selasih has served eight years. The board wants to keep her for six more years because she knows the bank well. Which statement fits BNM's expectations?
options: Tenure should generally not exceed nine years, except in exceptional cases or as a transition to succession plans
There is no limit; tenure is entirely a matter for shareholders
She must step down immediately, because BNM's limit on independent director tenure is eight years in total, without exceptions
She may stay if she is redesignated as an executive director
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.9 requires a disclosed tenure policy and says BNM expects independent director tenure generally not to exceed nine years, with narrow exceptions.

bank.question: An independent director's son has just become a partner in the audit firm that audits Selasih. What must happen under paragraph 11.10?
options: She must disclose it at once; the board reviews her designation and tells BNM its decision in writing
Nothing, because the external auditor is separately regulated and its partners' families are outside the board's concern
She must resign immediately without board review
The audit firm must be replaced so that she can stay independent
bank.explanation: An independent director must immediately disclose any change that may affect her independence; the board must then review the designation and notify BNM in writing of its decision to affirm or change it.

bank.question: Selasih's board risk management committee includes the bank's executive director as a member. Which statement is correct?
options: It is allowed if the executive director does not vote on matters concerning management
It is allowed because risk is a management matter
It is allowed if the committee is chaired by the board chairman
That is not allowed; only the nominations committee may include an executive director
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12.5 bars executive directors from board committees except the nominations committee (and a combined nominations and remuneration committee must have none). The board chairman cannot chair any committee.

bank.question: Selasih's board delegates approval of a large write-off to the board audit committee, which approves it. The write-off later proves improper. Who is accountable?
options: Only the audit committee members, because the decision was theirs under the delegation
Only the chief financial officer who proposed the write-off
The board, because it remains fully accountable for authority delegated to committees
Nobody, because the delegation was recorded in the board charter
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12.7 states that the board remains fully accountable for any authority it delegates to board committees.

bank.question: Which of these, required by BNM's Corporate Governance policy document, would most directly help a director meet the section 57 duty of care?
options: A rule that board papers are circulated on the morning of the meeting to keep their contents confidential
Attending at least half of board meetings in a financial year
Receiving relevant information on time and access to independent expert advice at the bank's cost
Relying on the CEO's summary instead of the full paper
bank.explanation: The chairman must make sure directors receive relevant information in time (9.1(b)), and the bank must provide access to third-party expert advice at its cost (9.7). The attendance minimum is 75%, not half.

bank.question: A partner of the firm that audited Selasih until last year is proposed as a director. What does paragraph 10.5 require?
options: He may join the board immediately if he formally declares his past audit role as a conflict of interest
He may join as long as he does not sit on the audit committee
He may join once BNM confirms he was not on the audit team
He cannot serve until at least two years after the firm last audited Selasih or he left the firm
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.5 bars officers involved in the engagement and any partner of the audit firm from becoming directors until at least two years after they leave the firm or the firm last served as auditor.

bank.question: Selasih announces a new director's appointment in a press release before BNM's written approval has arrived. What is wrong?
options: Nothing, as long as the director does not attend meetings yet
A bank must not publicly announce a proposed director appointment before BNM's written approval
Only the timing of the annual report disclosure is wrong
The press release should have named the nominations committee members
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.11(a) bars public announcement of a proposed director appointment without BNM's written approval, and section 54 requires prior written approval for the appointment itself.

bank.question: Selasih wants its new CEO to start on 1 October. When, at the latest, should the application reach BNM under Appendix 3?
options: By 1 July, at least three months before the expected start
By 1 September, one month before the CEO's planned start date
By 24 September, seven days before the start
Any time before the start, as BNM sets no timeline
bank.explanation: Appendix 3 requires an application at least three months before the individual is expected to take up the role.

bank.question: A director's term expires at the annual general meeting while his reappointment is still with BNM. What should he do?
options: Continue as a director for up to three months while BNM decides
Attend meetings as an observer and vote only on urgent items
Continue if shareholders voted for his reappointment at the meeting
Stop acting as a director, including at board meetings, until BNM approves the reappointment
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10.11(b) says a director whose tenure has expired and who is proposed for reappointment must immediately cease to hold office and act, including by not participating in board meetings, unless BNM's written approval has been obtained.

bank.question: Selasih's nominations committee assesses a CEO candidate who once resigned from another bank after questions about his expense claims. No charge was ever brought. How should the committee treat this?
options: As an automatic disqualification under section 59
As irrelevant, because no criminal charge was proven
As a financial integrity issue that requires a credit check only
As a probity factor to weigh with others, documenting why it is or is not decisive
bank.explanation: Resigning because of questions about honesty is a probity factor under paragraph 11.2. It is not a section 59 disqualification, and paragraph 10.4 says one failed factor is not automatically fatal; the reasoning must be recorded.

bank.question: Which body at Selasih must directly assess the fitness and propriety of the company secretary and decide on the appointment?
options: The CEO, under authority delegated by the board
The board and the nominations committee
The Companies Commission of Malaysia
The chief human resource officer
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8.1 makes the board and nominations committee directly responsible for assessing directors, the CEO and the company secretary. Only senior officer assessments may be delegated to the CEO or a designated committee.

bank.question: BNM tells Selasih that its Head of Wealth Management meets the definition of a senior officer but is missing from the key responsible persons list. What must Selasih do?
options: Explain to BNM in writing why the bank's own definition of senior officer is narrower
Change her job title so that she no longer meets the definition
Add her to the list and subject her to fit and proper assessments and requirements
Assess her once, but keep her off the list
bank.explanation: Paragraph 9.4 says that where BNM determines a person fulfils the definition but was not identified, the institution must include them and apply fit and proper assessments.

bank.question: Which statement best describes how a competency assessment of a Selasih director should take account of training?
options: Training is irrelevant once a director has a professional qualification
Training replaces experience, so a well-trained newcomer meets every competency need
Training matters only for executive directors and senior officers
Training is one of the competency factors weighed, alongside qualifications, skills, experience, commitment and time
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12.2 of the Fit and Proper Criteria policy document lists qualification, training, skills, practical experience and commitment, and for directors their other commitments.

bank.question: Selasih's annual board evaluation finds that two directors struggle with climate risk and digital banking topics. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Update each director's development plan, fund targeted training, and review the board's documented skill sets
Ask both directors to resign before the next evaluation
Record the finding and wait for BNM's comments
Appoint alternate directors with the missing expertise
bank.explanation: Paragraph 13.1 uses annual evaluations to find development needs, paragraph 13.3 requires budgets and updated development plans, and paragraph 11.2 requires skill sets to be reviewed. Alternate directors are not allowed.

bank.question: A senior officer of Selasih becomes an undischarged bankrupt. Under section 61, what must happen, and what compensation is due?
options: He must immediately cease to act, the bank must terminate the appointment, and he cannot claim compensation for that termination
He may continue until the board's next annual assessment, with full notice pay
The bank must suspend him on full pay until the bankruptcy ends
BNM must first confirm the disqualification before the bank acts
bank.explanation: Bankruptcy is a section 59(1) disqualification. Section 61 requires immediate cessation and termination, and section 61(3) removes any claim to compensation for that termination despite his contract.

bank.question: Why did BNM's press release on The Pacific Insurance Berhad mention the insurer's appointed representative and board oversight during the vacancy?
options: They were the reason BNM found the breach had not occurred
They were controls that kept operations from material disruption, considered among the case's facts and mitigating factors
They showed the insurer had obtained BNM approval for operating without a CEO
They were the cause of the vacancy, according to BNM
bank.explanation: BNM noted those controls prevented material disruption and said it considered aggravating and mitigating factors, yet still imposed RM336,000 because section 54 requires an approved CEO at all times.

bank.question: Selasih's management credit committee approves a large concentrated exposure that later fails. The Chief Risk Officer says, 'It was a committee decision, so it's not on me.' How does Responsibility Mapping view this?
options: The CRO is right, because collective decisions remove individual accountability
Committees continue, but the CRO remains accountable for his allocated risk management responsibility, including his role in that forum
Only the committee chair is accountable for committee decisions
The board becomes solely accountable for every committee decision
bank.explanation: Paragraph 1.6 says mapping exists in parallel with collective decision-making, and paragraph 7.16(f) requires documentation of responsibilities in collective forums. Allocated owners stay accountable.

bank.question: Selasih's CEO allocates AML/CFT/CPF policies and procedures to the Chief Compliance Officer without checking that she has the budget and staff to deliver them. Which requirement is most at risk?
options: Due diligence that the owner has the competence, authority and capability to fulfil the responsibility
Publication of the responsibility map on the bank's website
BNM's prior approval of every allocation
Annual rotation of all responsibilities to new owners to avoid complacency
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.6(a) requires due diligence on professional competence, authority and capabilities, and 7.10(d) expects the owner to ensure the area is adequately resourced. BNM does not pre-approve allocations.

bank.question: What must Selasih's board do to make sure the responsibility mapping framework changes behaviour, not just paperwork?
options: Publish each senior manager's responsibilities in the annual report
Require BNM to sign off each written acknowledgement
Rotate all senior managers between functions every year
Align performance, remuneration and consequence management frameworks with the mapping objective
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.2 requires the board to align performance, remuneration and consequence management frameworks with the goal of fostering good conduct by senior management.

bank.question: Selasih's new Head of Corporate Banking takes over from a colleague who moved to Singapore. The written acknowledgement is still signed by the predecessor. What should happen?
options: Nothing, because acknowledgements attach to the role not the person
Obtain a new acknowledgement from the new head and ensure an orderly handover is documented
Ask the predecessor to sign the acknowledgement again from Singapore as the last owner
Wait for the next annual refresh of all acknowledgements
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.17 requires acknowledgement at appointment and on significant changes, and 7.10(e) expects orderly transition when responsibilities are reallocated.

bank.question: Which of these is an example BNM gives of a senior manager failing to act with integrity under Responsibility Mapping?
options: Omitting to act on a material misstatement that she knows about
Missing a project deadline because of an IT supplier's delay
Disagreeing with the CEO in a management committee
Delegating a task to a competent and supervised deputy
bank.explanation: Footnote 6 to paragraph 7.9 gives examples such as authorising or omitting to act on material misstatement, failing to address conflicts of interest, and acting dishonestly against customers or the institution.

bank.question: Selasih wants to keep its responsibility documentation brief. Which element is required by paragraph 7.14, beyond listing the responsibilities?
options: A list of every staff member in the manager's division with their salaries
The manager's personal financial statements for the past three years
A clear description of how the manager must support the bank's outcomes, including the actions, decisions and outcomes they own
A statement from the external auditor confirming each responsibility
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.14 requires the documentation to articulate responsibilities and the institution's expectation of how the manager supports outcomes, identifying the actions, decisions and outcomes they are responsible for.

bank.question: Selasih decides that the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Risk Officer will co-lead the treasury function. Which documentation point applies to this shared role?
options: A ruling from BNM on which of them is senior
An explanation of whether their responsibilities in that role are identical or differ
A requirement that only one of them signs an acknowledgement
A statement that neither is accountable until the board decides
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.16(d) requires, for a shared role, an explanation of whether responsibilities are identical or differ between the individuals; shared responsibilities make each jointly and severally accountable.

bank.question: BNM asks Selasih for the documentation of responsibilities of its senior management. What must the bank do?
options: Refuse, because the documentation is internal and confidential
Make the documentation available to BNM on request
Provide only a summary approved by the board audit committee
Provide it only after BNM issues a formal enforcement notice
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.18 requires the institution to make the documentation available to BNM upon request.

bank.question: Selasih's whistleblowing policy says concerns go 'to the appropriate person'. What is the weakness under paragraph 18.2(a)?
options: It fails to require that every concern is also reported to the police
It allows staff to report without involving their line manager
It does not clearly indicate the parties within the bank to whom concerns can be escalated
It does not set a minimum value for the misconduct reported
bank.explanation: Paragraph 18.2(a) requires the policy to clearly indicate the internal parties to whom concerns can be escalated. A vague reference to 'the appropriate person' fails that test.

bank.question: The designated non-executive director asks for whistleblowing statistics every quarter and commissions a review of the policy every two years. Is she going beyond what BNM expects?
options: No; evaluating periodic reports and overseeing periodic reviews of effectiveness are part of her responsibility
Yes; her role is limited to receiving reports that concern the CEO and other directors of the bank
Yes; reviewing the policy is a matter for management only
No, but only because BNM requires a review every two years
bank.explanation: The footnote to paragraph 18.2(d) says the designated director's role includes evaluating periodic reports on how concerns are escalated and handled, and overseeing periodic reviews. BNM sets no specific two-year interval.

bank.question: Selasih's code of ethics breach register is empty for three years in a 4,000-staff bank, though HR has disciplined several staff for conflicts of interest. What does this suggest?
options: The bank's culture is excellent, which BNM will welcome
Breaches are not being recorded as paragraph 18.1 requires, which weakens evidence of culture
The register is optional guidance, so it does not matter
Only breaches reported to BNM need to be recorded
bank.explanation: Paragraph 18.1 requires the bank to maintain a record of breaches of the code of ethics and address them with integrity. Disciplinary cases for conflicts that never reach the register point to a gap.

bank.question: An employee of Selasih takes part in a scheme to inflate sales figures, then reports it to BNM to protect himself. Under the exclusions BNM describes, what is likely?
options: He keeps full protection because he reported first
He gains immunity from disciplinary action by the bank
His whistleblower protection may be revoked because he participated in the improper conduct
BNM must reject the report and take no action
bank.explanation: BNM's page lists participation in the disclosed improper conduct as a ground for revoking or excluding protection. The information can still be investigated.

bank.question: A Selasih intern sees a supervisor altering customer signatures on loan forms. The intern is unsure whether interns may use the whistleblowing channel. What should the bank's policy already have ensured?
options: That interns report only through their university coordinator
That interns wait until they become permanent staff
That the policy was communicated to interns and that they are allowed to report concerns
That interns may report only matters involving other interns
bank.explanation: Paragraph 18.2(c) requires the policy to be communicated to third parties such as contractors, consultants and interns and to allow them to report.

bank.question: Which practice best shows Selasih that staff can raise concerns 'in confidence and without the risk of reprisal'?
options: Telling the person reported on who made the report so they can respond fairly
Limiting knowledge of the reporter's identity to need-to-know and checking for adverse treatment after a report
Requiring reporters to sign a statement accepting any consequences
Allowing reports only after a line manager has approved them
bank.explanation: Paragraph 18.2 requires confidential reporting without risk of reprisal. Need-to-know handling of identity and monitoring for detriment put that into practice; revealing the reporter or requiring manager approval undermines it.

bank.question: Selasih's compliance team learns from a whistleblowing report that a regional head manipulated complaint data sent to the board. Under paragraph 16.1, what is senior management's duty?
options: Wait until the year-end audit before telling the board
Handle the case within the region to avoid wider disruption
Address the actual or suspected breach promptly and keep the board informed of material control failures
Report the matter only if BNM's supervisors ask about it
bank.explanation: Paragraph 16.1(d) and (e) make senior management responsible for addressing breaches in a timely and appropriate way and for updating the board on material matters such as internal control failures.

bank.question: A Selasih manager reports to BNM a concern that he knows is untrue, to damage a rival. What does BNM's whistleblowing page say?
options: He keeps protection because the report was made in writing
BNM simply ignores it with no consequence for him
Knowingly making a false disclosure is a criminal offence under the Whistleblower Protection Act 2010
Only the bank can take action, through its code of ethics
bank.explanation: BNM states that a person who makes a disclosure knowing or believing material statements to be false commits an offence under the Whistleblower Protection Act 2010, and such reports lose protection.

bank.question: An employee of Selasih complains that a customer's representative sexually harassed her during a meeting at a branch. Who can be the subject of a complaint under Part XVA of the Employment Act?
options: Any person at all, including customers and visitors
Only the employer, never a fellow employee
Only employees who earn RM4,000 a month or less
Only an employee or the employer; for others the employer can still act through its own policies and other laws
bank.explanation: Section 81A defines a complaint as one by an employee against an employee or the employer, or by the employer against an employee. Harassment by a customer falls outside Part XVA, though the bank should still protect staff, and the Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022 Tribunal is open to any person.

bank.question: The Director General of Labour directs Selasih to inquire into a complaint it had refused. What must Selasih do next?
options: Carry out the inquiry and submit its report to the Director General within 30 days of the direction
Appeal to BNM against the direction, since banks are supervised by BNM rather than by Labour
Hold the inquiry within six months and keep the report internal
Ask the complainant to withdraw so the direction lapses
bank.explanation: Section 81D(2) requires the employer to inquire when directed and report to the Director General within 30 days. Failing to do so is an offence under section 81F.

bank.question: Selasih's inquiry finds harassment proven against a contractor working on its premises, not an employee. What does section 81C say the employer should do?
options: Dismiss the contractor without notice under the Employment Act
Recommend that the person be brought before the disciplinary authority they are subject to
Downgrade the contractor's role on the project
Take no action, because the inquiry has no effect on non-employees
bank.explanation: Section 81C(b) says that where the person complained against is not an employee, the employer recommends that they be brought before an appropriate disciplinary authority. The bank can also act under its contract.

bank.question: A Selasih employee in Kuching asks whether the Employment Act 1955 governs her sexual harassment complaint. What is the accurate starting point?
options: The Act applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan, so she should check the labour law that applies in Sarawak
The Act applies to every state, so it governs her complaint in full
No employment law applies; only the bank's internal policy does
Only BNM's rules apply, because she works for a bank
bank.explanation: Section 1(2) applies the Act to Peninsular Malaysia only, and it has been extended to Labuan. Staff in Sabah and Sarawak need to check the labour law that applies there; the Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022 is a federal route for anyone.

bank.question: BNM finds that Selasih breached a policy document requirement. Selasih did not self-report, but cooperated fully and fixed the root cause quickly. Which is the most realistic expectation?
options: No penalty can be imposed once the breach has been fixed
The penalty will be doubled because the breach was not self-reported
Cooperation and effective remediation may mitigate the penalty, while the lack of self-reporting is a missed mitigating factor
BNM must prosecute in court because the breach was not self-reported
bank.explanation: BNM's Enforcement Approach treats cooperation, voluntary reporting and effective remediation as post-misconduct factors. Fixing a breach does not erase it, and BNM sets no automatic multiplier.

bank.question: Selasih receives notice that BNM has imposed an administrative monetary penalty. The bank believes the facts are wrong. What avenue does BNM's Enforcement Approach describe?
options: Appeal directly to the Federal Court within 90 days
Make written representations to BNM and, if still aggrieved, appeal to the Monetary Penalty Review Committee within 21 days
Ask the Securities Commission to review BNM's decision
Pay the penalty and seek a refund through BNMLINK
bank.explanation: BNM communicates its decision with an opportunity for written representation, and an aggrieved person may appeal to the MPRC within 21 days of being notified.

bank.question: Which pairing correctly matches a Malaysian requirement to its source in this quest?
options: Written acknowledgement of senior management responsibilities: FSA section 62
Designated non-executive director for whistleblowing: Fit and Proper Criteria policy document
Seven-day notice to BNM when a director leaves: Responsibility Mapping paragraph 7.17
Sexual harassment awareness notice at the workplace: Employment Act 1955, section 81H
bank.explanation: Section 81H sets the notice duty. Acknowledgements come from Responsibility Mapping paragraph 7.17, the designated director from Corporate Governance paragraph 18.2(d), and the seven-day notice from FSA section 62.

bank.question: Selasih prepares for BNM's governance review. Which set of evidence best shows that its governance is working in practice rather than on paper?
options: Minutes showing challenge, signed responsibility acknowledgements, fit and proper records with reasons, and whistleblowing and harassment case logs
A long board charter, a new logo for the code of ethics and a staff survey score
The CEO's statement that the bank has never had a governance breach
Copies of BNM's policy documents filed in each department
bank.explanation: BNM looks for evidence: minutes that record deliberation and dissent, acknowledgements under paragraph 7.17, documented assessments, and records showing concerns and complaints are handled. Statements and copies of rules prove little.
